This is a special City Council meeting, starting with the canvass of the votes, then moving onto public comment and Council business.

Below are my preliminary thoughts and initial positions going into the meeting. Please email me at <sjacobson@franklinnh.gov> if you would like to discuss further. 


There will be public hearings on agenda items 2 through 9 prior to Council discussion. You can also submit public comment before the meeting or if you cannot be present on the [city website](https://franklin-service-requests-39a5.vercel.app/?page=public-input).

## 2. Grant Funding for Schools
- Summary: 
    - Total funds below are $550,044. 
    - $200,000 from NH Dept of Education Safe and Supportive Schools for social and emotional wellness of students. 
    - $255,000 from Crotched Mountain Foundation for the development of the lakes region special education consortium.
    - $44,200 from David M Brooks Music Education Program for music programs. 
    - $28,478 from the Special Education Capital Reserve fund for special education costs in FY27. 
    - $22,365 from School Facilities Capital Reserve Fund for facilities costs in FY27. 

### How Sam Sees It: 
- We should accept these funds. 
- Building school functions on grants is not sustainable in the long term, however we should accept these at this time. 

## 3.  School Fund Balance
- Summary: 
    - School district spent $87,295 over budget in FY 26. 
    - School district took in $178,286 over revenue in FY 26. 
    - This uses the extra revenue to cover the extra expenses, leaving $90,991 in fund balance for FY27. 
    - This money is found via 'clean up' at the end of the year - invoices and contracts that do not match budget. 
 

### How Sam Sees It:
- We should use the school revenue to pay for the school expenditures and accept this proposal. 

## 4. Paving North Main Street
- Summary:
    - $289,174 to pave ~3,800 ft. of road from Benson's to Webster Lake Road. 
    - Money to come from Municipal Transport Improvement Fund.

### How Sam Sees It:
- North Main St. water service pipes are scheduled for conversion from 10" to 12" in the CIP. I don't want to pave only to rip it up again. 
- I'm concerned this plan will pave North Main, then rip it up again to replace piping. 

## 5. Paving Davis, Birch, and Jason Streets
- Summary:
    - $54,922 to pave Davis, Birch, and Jason streets. 
    - Money to come from Municipal Transportation Improvement Fund. 

### How Sam Sees It:
- I think we should pave these roads. 

## 6. Purchasing New MSD Equipment
- Summary: 
    - Pay $22,700 for the following items:
        - Trailer
        - Truck body
        - Pavement saw
        - Plate compactor plate
    - Money to come from the FY27 Budget ($5,500) and MSD capital reserve ($17,200).
 
### How Sam Sees it: 
- I think we should have at least 3 quotes for the trailer and truck body, given that they are more than $5,000.

## 7. Solid Waste Ordinance
- Summary: 
    - Change code to allow for sticker system for trash pickup.
        - Stickers are:
            - $65 for a small (48 gallon barrel)
            - $90 for a medium (64 gallon barrel)
            - $125 for a large (96 gallon barrel)
            - $1.25/20 lbs of trash at the transfer station

### How Sam Sees It: 
- This aligns the code with the budget for this year. 
- We need to implement this system in order to balance the city budget this year. 
- I'd like to set a minimum fee to drive over the scale, especially for lower volumes of trash. (e.g. $1 to drive over the scale).  

## 8. Proposed Tax Cap Amendment to Legal Council - Clarifications

- Summary:
    - This proposal is similar to the amendment proposed at the June 1 City Council meeting. 
    - Seeks to trigger the charter amendment process.
        - The charter amendment process begins with a Council vote, then moves to a public hearing, then a state officials' review.
    - This amendment would clarify that costs outside of the tax cap (e.g. capital costs) are not included in the next year's calculations. 

### How Sam Sees It: 
- I understand the desire to add this language; however, I do not think it is necessary. The Council can always approve a budget beneath the tax cap (i.e. manually remove the capital costs from the previous year). 
- Moving ongoing exempted expenditures (e.g. bond payments) outside the tax cap calculation one year and under the tax cap the next would make budgeting difficult, if not impossible. 

## 9. Proposed Tax Cap Amendment to Legal Council - Reassessments

- Summary:
    - This is similar to the amendment proposed at the June 1 City Council meeting. 
    - Seeks to trigger the  charter amendment process.
        - The charter amendment process begins with a Council vote, then moves to a public hearing, then a state officials' review.
    - Amendment adds maximum 3% additional increase every 5 years.
        - This change accounts for differences in inflation and other unforeseen costs. 
        - If this were implemented in the FY 27 budget, property taxes could have increased $608,594 (3%) in addition to the $711,298 (3.5%). 


### How Sam Sees It: 
- Because these increases are only possible to be made every 5 years, it tends to lead to years with big hits. I think shrinking the length of time and tightening the exception (e.g. max 1%, every 2 years) would smooth tax changes. 
- As written, this may require accounting for 3% over multiple years, which could be confusing (i.e. what is the base year for calculating the changes?).
- This could be sequenced to align with off-year elections to enhance their importance and focus for the community. 

## 10. City Manager Evaluation
- Summary: 
    - Council to set a non-public meeting to establish criteria for City Manager evaluation.
    - No standard or rubric for City Manager performance has been established. 
    - Proposal set before the Council: One week before the evaluation meeting, the Council submits materials for consideration by the Council as a whole. 
    
### How Sam Sees it: 
- We should set and establish evaluation criteria.
